newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Clinton brings Kohl to tears with memories.
newsitem.headline: Clinton brings Kohl to tears with memories.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton brought Helmut Kohl to tears on Wednesday, evoking the German chancellor's childhood memories of the way America helped rebuild his war-shattered homeland.

Television cameras and photographers captured Kohl struggling vainly to hold back his emotions as Clinton, in a speech marking the 50th anniversary of the Marshall Plan, cited him as the spirit of Europe's rebirth.

"For a teenage boy in Germany, Marshall aid was the generous hand that helped lift his homeland from the ruinous past. He still recalls American trucks driving onto the schoolyard, bring soup that warmed hands and hearts," Clinton said.
"That boy grew up to be a passionate champion of freedom and unity in Europe, a great and cherished friend of America. He became the first chancellor of a free and unified Germany.
"Helmut Kohl has come to symbolise both the substance and spirit of the Marshall plan," Clinton said.
